newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA RAISES STAKE SOLD FOR BAD LOAN BONDS.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA RAISES STAKE SOLD FOR BAD LOAN BONDS.

text.p: Bulgaria's interim cabinet on Thursday raised the stake in local state firms that can be paid in with bad loan bonds or Zunks, in privatisation deals to 80 percent from 50 percent so far.
"The government allowed the payment of up to 80 percent of the price of privatised medium and small state enterprises in Zunks and 20 percent in cash," a press centre official said.
Until now Zunks were accepted as a means of payment of up to 50 percent of the price.
Foreign investors have shown growing interest in dollar-denominated Zunks because they can be used as a means of payment in sell-offs of state companies at par value.
Bad debt bonds worth 32 billion levs and $1.8 billion respectively were issued three years ago to cover banks' non-performing loans extended to state companies before 1991.
Their minimum acceptable prices are now set at 35 and 45 percent of par, respectively.
There were $939.6 million and 20 billion levs of bad debt bonds in circulation by the end of March, figures showed.
Foreign investors have bought Bulgarian government securities worth 47 billion levs and $100 million between the beginning of March and April 11, a central bank official said recently.
The cabinet's first steps towards speeding up sell-offs to raise desperately needed cash, have also boosted Zunk trade.
The BNB has sold 15.2 billion levs of lev-denominated Zunks from its portfolio in the first week of April.
The scheme does not apply to big factories expected to be privatised this year. Bulgaria expects 300-350 million dollars from the sale of these firms, the government's press-office said.
The cabinet has decided to assign some big sell-offs to international investment banks instead of the privatisation agency, which so far has been too slow.
